data.name: Octaviel
data.gender_notes: Octaviel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman numeral octo, meaning 'eight', Octaviel is a name of Latin origin with a connection to the Bible. In the New Testament, the name Octavian is given to a Roman soldier who converts to Christianity after encountering St. Peter and St. Paul. This name holds a deep spiritual significance, representing the eighth day or the eighth day of creation, a time of new beginnings and renewed faith. Octaviel is a strong and faithful name, a symbol of courage and wisdom, carrying with it a sense of deep rooted loyalty and compassion.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes new beginnings and renewed faith
data.etymology: Octaviel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Eighth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Octaviel total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: אוקטאויאל

in_greek.name: ΟκταβIEL
in_greek.long_meaning: ΟκταβIEL είναι το όνομα που προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη Octavus, που σημαίνει 'ο όγδοος', και το επίθημα el, που έχει εβραϊκή ρίζα και σημαίνει 'Θεός' ή 'άγγελος', υποδηλώνοντας σύνδεση με τη θεότητα, και στην χριστιανική παράδοση αντιπροσωπεύει αγιότητα και θείο έργο

in_latin.name: Octaviel

historical_references.reference: The Golden Legend: A Devotional Literature in Late Medieval Europe. Book V, Chapter 25. Octavian and Octavie.
historical_references.context: Octavian was a Roman military commander who was converted to Christianity by Saint Agnes. He married a Christian woman named Octavie, and they both underwent persecution and martyrdom for their faith during the Diocletian Persecution (AD 303-311).

historical_references.reference: Butler's Lives of the Saints: A Complete English Translation. Volume II, October, page 865. Octavian and Octavie.
historical_references.context: Octavian was a Roman soldier who was converted to Christianity at the insistence of his wife, Octavie. They suffered persecution during the reign of Emperor Maximian (late 3rd century). Octavian was martyred, and Octavie, who was pregnant at the time, died by suicide to avoid being forced into prostitution.
